page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: The hybridisation
lines: In the carbonate ion CO₃²⁻ the carbon
Carbon is bonded to three oxygen atoms
and carries no lone pair, so it needs
One 2s orbital and two 2p orbitals mix
steps.why: The number of hybrid orbitals a carbon atom needs is the number of atoms bonded to it plus the number of lone pairs on it. In the carbonate ion that number is three, so one s orbital and two p orbitals are mixed and the hybridisation is sp².
common_mistakes: Answering sp³ because carbon has four valence electrons. The count that fixes the hybridisation is the three bonded oxygen atoms, not the electron count.
Counting a double bond as two bonded atoms. A double bond joins carbon to one oxygen atom, so the count of bonded atoms is still three.
steps.memory_tip: Three bonded atoms and no lone pair means sp².
steps.margin_note: State sp², then give the count of three bonded oxygen atoms as the reason.

steps.label: Shape and the fourth orbital
lines: The three sp² orbitals lie in one plane
at 120° to one another, so the ion is
stands at right angles to that plane.
It forms a pi bond that is spread over

lines.text: Carbon is sp²; the CO₃²⁻ ion is planar

steps.why: Three sp² orbitals point to the corners of an equilateral triangle, so the ion is flat and the O–C–O angles are 120°. The 2p orbital left over is what makes the pi bond, and because that pi bond is spread over all three oxygen atoms the three C–O bonds are of equal length.
common_mistakes: Calling the carbonate ion pyramidal. Three sp² orbitals lie in one plane, so the ion is flat.
Drawing one short double bond and two long single bonds. The pi bond is spread over all three oxygen atoms, so the three C–O bonds are equal.
steps.memory_tip: sp² gives a flat triangle with 120° angles.
steps.margin_note: Add the shape and the 120° angle after naming the hybridisation.

insider_note: The answer itself is one word, sp², so a complete answer also gives the count of three bonded oxygen atoms and the flat shape with 120° angles.
